summary.en: The four words you will hear in almost every business conversation.
summary.bs: Četiri riječi koje ćeš čuti u skoro svakom poslovnom razgovoru.

concepts.youtubeQuery: what is revenue in business explained simply

en.one: Revenue is all the money a business gets from selling, before paying any costs.
en.explain: People also call it sales or turnover. It is the top line: the first number you look at. Nothing has been taken away from it yet.
en.example: A café sells 1,000 coffees at €2 each in a month. Its revenue is €2,000.
en.why: Revenue shows how much customers want what you sell. But high revenue alone does not mean the business is doing well.
en.mixup: Revenue is not profit. A business can have huge revenue and still lose money if costs are even bigger.

bs.one: Revenue (prihod) je sav novac koji firma dobije od prodaje, prije nego plati ikakve troškove.
bs.explain: Zove se još i promet ili prodaja. To je prva linija: prvi broj koji gledaš. Od njega još ništa nije oduzeto.
bs.example: Kafić u mjesecu proda 1.000 kafa po 2 €. Njegov prihod je 2.000 €.
bs.why: Prihod pokazuje koliko kupci žele ono što prodaješ. Ali sam veliki prihod ne znači da firma dobro posluje.
bs.mixup: Prihod nije dobit. Firma može imati ogroman prihod i svejedno gubiti novac ako su troškovi još veći.

en.one: A cost is money a business spends to make and sell its product.
en.explain: Costs include materials, rent, wages, electricity, marketing and more. Some costs come with every sale, like coffee beans. Others stay the same every month, like rent.
en.example: For each €2 coffee, the café spends €0.50 on beans, milk and a cup. On top of that it pays €800 rent each month.
en.why: You can only make money if you know your costs. Many businesses fail because they guess costs instead of counting them.
en.mixup: A cost is not always a bad thing. Spending on a good ad can bring in much more revenue.

bs.one: Cost (trošak) je novac koji firma potroši da napravi i proda svoj proizvod.
bs.explain: Troškovi su materijal, kirija, plate, struja, reklama i drugo. Neki troškovi dolaze sa svakom prodajom, npr. kafa u zrnu. Drugi su isti svaki mjesec, npr. kirija.
bs.example: Za svaku kafu od 2 € kafić potroši 0,50 € na kafu, mlijeko i čašu. Uz to plaća 800 € kirije mjesečno.
bs.why: Možeš zarađivati samo ako znaš svoje troškove. Mnoge firme propadnu jer troškove nagađaju umjesto da ih broje.
bs.mixup: Trošak nije uvijek loš. Novac potrošen na dobru reklamu može donijeti mnogo veći prihod.

en.one: Margin is how much of each sale you keep after paying for what you sold.
en.explain: It is usually shown as a percentage of the price. A high margin means you keep a big part of each sale. A low margin means you need to sell a lot to earn anything.
en.example: You sell a coffee for €2. It costs you €0.50 to make. You keep €1.50, which is a 75% margin.
en.why: Margin tells you how much room you have to pay rent, wages and still make profit.
en.mixup: Margin is not the same as markup. Markup compares profit to the cost (€1.50 ÷ €0.50 = 300%). Margin compares it to the price (75%).

bs.one: Margin (marža) je koliko od svake prodaje zadržiš nakon što platiš ono što si prodao.
bs.explain: Obično se prikazuje kao postotak od cijene. Visoka marža znači da zadržiš veliki dio svake prodaje. Niska marža znači da moraš puno prodati da bi išta zaradio.
bs.example: Prodaješ kafu za 2 €. Tebe košta 0,50 € da je napraviš. Zadržiš 1,50 €, što je marža od 75%.
bs.why: Marža ti govori koliko prostora imaš da platiš kiriju, plate i da ti još ostane dobit.
bs.mixup: Marža nije isto što i markup (dodatak na cijenu). Markup poredi zaradu s troškom (1,50 € ÷ 0,50 € = 300%). Marža je poredi s cijenom (75%).

formula.en: Break-even units = Fixed costs ÷ (Price − Cost per unit)
formula.bs: Količina za pokriće = Fiksni troškovi ÷ (Cijena − Trošak po komadu)

en.one: Break-even is the point where you have earned exactly enough to cover all your costs.
en.explain: Below break-even you lose money. Above it, every extra sale is profit. It answers the question: how much do I need to sell just to not lose money?
en.example: The café pays €800 rent a month and keeps €1.50 from every coffee. €800 ÷ €1.50 ≈ 534 coffees. Once it sells about 534 coffees, the rent is covered and every coffee after that is profit.
en.why: Before starting anything, knowing your break-even tells you if the idea is realistic.
en.mixup: Breaking even is not success. It only means you are not losing money yet.

bs.one: Break-even (tačka pokrića) je trenutak kad si zaradio tačno toliko da pokriješ sve troškove.
bs.explain: Ispod tačke pokrića gubiš novac. Iznad nje, svaka dodatna prodaja je dobit. Odgovara na pitanje: koliko moram prodati samo da ne bih bio u minusu?
bs.example: Kafić plaća 800 € kirije mjesečno i od svake kafe zadrži 1,50 €. 800 € ÷ 1,50 € ≈ 534 kafe. Kad proda oko 534 kafe, kirija je pokrivena, a svaka kafa nakon toga je dobit.
bs.why: Prije nego išta pokreneš, tačka pokrića ti govori da li je ideja realna.
bs.mixup: Doći do tačke pokrića nije uspjeh. To samo znači da još ne gubiš novac.
